court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Manish Prabhakar Nikam vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Maharashtra And Another

facts_of_case: Parties have arrived at amicable settlement. Husband seeks quashing of FIR and proceedings.

legal_principles.principle: The power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
legal_principles.held: The position that emerges from the above discussion can be summarised thus: the power of the High Court in quashing a criminal proceeding or FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction is distinct and different from the power given to a criminal court for compounding the offences under Section 320 of the Code.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Kulwinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2007) 4 CTC 769

legal_principles.principle: The High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime before exercising its power to quash a criminal proceeding or complaint or FIR.
legal_principles.held: Before exercise of such power, the High Court must have due regard to the nature and gravity of the crime.
cited_cases: Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab and others, (2012) 10 SCC 303
Kulwinder Singh v. State of Punjab (2007) 4 CTC 769
keywords: nature and gravity of the crime

outcome.final_order: Quashing of FIR and proceedings allowed.
